“I…I don’t know how to say this.”
She watched his thumb sweep over her knuckles. Once. Twice. The familiar lines of his tattoos, the flex of his tendons, and the roughness of his palms.
Say it. Just say it.

“Actually,” Korra said, “He’s one of mine. I’m the Avatar after him.” And then figuring she might as well drop the pretenses, Korra metalbended the cuffs off of herself and waved, hoping what once would have been an easy feat of bending didn’t make her visibly sweat. “Hi.”

summary:
One year after the first plague wave nearly destroyed Ba Sing Se, the city begins to breathe again. The bells slow. The death carts lighten. Survivors cautiously reopen markets and homes while Khione, Katara, Sokka, Aang, Toph, and the Dai Li continue patrols beneath the shadow of lingering infection.
But the peace is temporary.
When coughing returns to Stoneflower Market, Khione realizes the plague has evolved. The second wave spreads not through explosive collapse, but through breath, contact, and routine. Pneumonic plague moves quietly through reopened streets, delivery routes, crowded homes, and hidden carriers. The city does not fall into chaos this time. Instead, Ba Sing Se enters a long war of detection, isolation, and endurance. As months pass, the plague doctors become a permanent part of the city. The Dai Li transform from secret police into containment wardens. Sokka builds tracking systems. Katara learns to heal within impossible limits. And Khione becomes known across the city as its doctor.
By the end of the year, the plague has not vanished. But Ba Sing Se has learned how to survive it.

summary:
The Avatar is dead.
The war should have ended with Sozin’s Comet. Instead, it became something else.
Ten years later, the Phoenix Empire controls the world through occupation, surveillance, and a system that tracks benders by bloodline. No element is safe. Under the guise of unity, the Empire has begun enforcing arranged marriages between citizens and benders; binding power, loyalty, and lineage into something it can monitor, control, and, if necessary, eliminate.
The resistance survives in fragments. Katara survives by refusing to look back. She does not think about the boy who believed in balance. She does not think about the war that never ended. And she does not think about the prince who chose the other side.
Some things don’t stay buried.
When her name appears on the Empire’s registry, survival is no longer enough. Pulled into a system designed to control power, and the people who carry it. Katara is forced to navigate shifting alliances, impossible choices, and a past that refuses to remain where she left it.

It felt like his skin was on fire.
Not the kind of fire that he'd bend. Not the kind of fire that had scarred his face.
It was a fire made from attendants doing every conceivable thing to prepare him for today. It was a fire made from embarrassment and anxiety.

Keep your composure.

All of this for an alpha he had never met. All of this for a political plot his father had come up with. 
All of this because of the Southern Water Tribe.

Katara could have made her words sound like a threat - as she did every time she spoke to him. But it wasn't the tone nor the volume that gave it away. It was that one word that made the difference.
Us.
There was no ‚us’ between her and Zuko. There never had been. To hear her say that they were part of something together … why did that thought make his stomach feel so strange?
"No, I don't mind," he replied simply. He sounded unimpressed, but it was raging in his head. Change was in the air, as heavy and thick as the steam from a hot spring.
He couldn't see it with his eyes, but he could feel it.
--
Zuko finally joined Team Avatar at the Southern Air Temple and has yet anything but arrived. Most of the group members still don’t trust him. Especially one particular waterbender that watches his every move.
One day, Zuko discovers a secret hot spring inside the tempels. It becomes his sanctuary – a place just to himself. Or so he thought.

summary:
Water. Earth. Fire. Air.
Alpha. Beta. Omega.
My grandmother used to tell me stories about the old days. A time of peace, when the Avatar kept balance between the Water Tribe, Earth Kingdom, Fire Nation, and Air Nomads, and between the Natures that shaped all of society. But that all changed when the Fire Nation attacked.
Only the Avatar mastered all four elements, and kept alpha guardianship, beta integrity, and omega devotion in harmony. But when the Fire Nation struck, they shattered that natural order. Only he could stop the ruthless firebenders from crushing all beneath their rule. But when the world needed him most, he vanished.
A hundred years have passed, and the Fire Nation is nearing victory in the war. Two years ago, my father and the last of our warriors and hunters journeyed to the Earth Kingdom to help fight against the Fire Nation, leaving me and my brother to hold our tribe together. Some people believe that the Avatar was never reborn into the Air Nomads, and that the cycle was broken. But I haven't lost hope. I still believe that somehow, someday, the Avatar will return to restore balance to the elements, and bring a new unity to our bonds.

title: love is the one thing we're capable of perceiving that transcends dimensions of time and space

summary:
The reason Convergence existed was Sozin's Comet. Not the night of impact, three hundred years ago, though that had been catastrophic immediately, half of the Air Nomad population disintegrating from impact, most of the Earth Kingdom burning, the sky was tinted red for weeks, the kind of event that showed up in every history curriculum and every cultural memory. The long term issue was atmospheric. The comet's impact had disrupted climate systems and the ozone layer that was said to be irreparable, and it occurs slowly across centuries, compounding in ways the Republic City science division had been tracking for decades and finally releasing to the public five years ago. The data was not good. Their planet was dying, not quickly, not visibly, not in a single lifetime, but the projections kept moving in one direction no matter how many times people checked the math, and the Global Government had eventually decided that the answer was not to wait it out.
Hence P-1. Hence the Appa. Hence the blue wax envelope.

“Summers at Ember Island were a royal family favorite. With its relaxing ocean waves, soft-sanded beaches, and its hot sun blaring down for long hours at a time, the island never failed to rejuvenate even the most stressed-out individual. They included Kanto, too, broad-shouldered and kind in the way mountains were, sitting beside Toph with his feet buried in the sand. "There is no Lady Tomoe on this manifest," the officer barked, his voice grating and thin behind the eye-slits. "The household has been dissolved by royal decree. It is just Tomoe now. Move the cargo to the lower steerage deck with the rest of the crew's rations."
Three days ago, Tomoe was destined for the Fire Nation throne. Yesterday, her family was executed for treason, their names erased for supporting a teenage prince's outburst in a war council. Today, she is a nameless exile on a disgraced ship, staring at the scarred boy whose words cost her everything.
Stripped of her title, Tomoe is taken aboard the Wani by General Iroh, the last remaining link to the future she was groomed to inherit. Trapped on a rusted vessel with a volatile, mutilated prince, her courtly education is reduced to a tool for basic survival. But as the hopeless search for the Avatar drags into years, the shared isolation of their exile begins to forge something far more dangerous than hatred.
An epic, (mature/explicit) slow-burn exploration of political survival, grief, and a changing world. Spanning from the first day of exile, through the war, and into their adult years.

“Fire Lord Zuko?”  The Grand Chamberlain inquired, and from his tone, Zuko gathered it was not the first time he had called out for his attention.
“Yes, Grand Chamberlain?”
“What did you want to do in regards to the Southern Water Tribe’s request?”
“The request?” Zuko asked, well aware it was already too late to pretend he had been listening.
“The Southern Water Tribe requests your presence for the grand opening of their first school…. That they plan on naming it in honor of you, Fire Lord Zuko,” The Grand Chamberlain’s face was contorted in a funny way, very obviously fighting for his life to look as unannoyed as possible.
“In my…honor?” Zuko’s eyebrow raised in surprise, and he was sure he had not heard right.
“Yes, my Lord” The Grand Chamberlain was again struggling to keep his face schooled into neutrality, although a twitch in his left eye was about to be his undoing, “ and Master Katara has requested your presence…” Zuko suddenly felt like the floor had fallen out from underneath him.
“So, Fire Lord Zuko, what is your answer?”

summary:
Zuko has been having dreams on and off about a life he knows he's never lived. When he's asleep, it feels so real, especially the love he feels for a mysterious woman. When he wakes up, he can't remember anything but the way that he's felt about her. But he knows it can't be true. He's never felt anything like that in his life and he never expects to feel anything like that. A good life for him would be continuing the stability of working for his family's company.
But that changes the moment he sees Katara.
Katara has lived a long time, seeing lifetimes go by, watching humanity change. While she enjoys the experiences her temporary time of incarnation brings, she's always kept herself distant from anything even resembling love. Feeling the loss of the only person she's ever loved once was more than enough for her eternity. But meeting Zuko changed that.

title: Spring of the Drowned Blind Earthbender
author: SkittyCat
characters: Other Character Tags to Be Added
summary:
It was like someone had turned off the sun.
He didn’t know how long he sunk for until he finally felt the bottom of the pool with his butt. But he finally had a way to orient himself. Getting his feet underneath him, he pushed and frantically swam for what he hoped was up.
He couldn’t tell how long he was under the water, thoughts as muddled with panic as they were. It could’ve been seconds, minutes, hours or even days.
His despair reached new heights when he broke the surface, desperately sputtering and gasping for breath. Automatically, he began to tread water while his hands went to scrub at his eyes, hoping that whatever it was that was preventing him from seeing would go away if he did.
But nothing changed, no matter how hard he scrubbed.
This was wrong. Seriously, seriously wrong. Why couldn’t he see?
Why couldn’t he see?!

summary: Toph and her father have rebuilt their relationship and the Metalbending Academy has been very successful. Only there's one piece missing. Her mother. Could she still live at the estate in Gaoling? Toph didn't know. But she never got that "life changing field trip with Zuko." Maybe now was the time.Toph stomped toward the academy entrance, grabbed a blank sheet of paper from the front desk, and slapped it flat onto the stone floor beside Ho Tun. “There,” she said. “Write.”He grabbed the ink brush carefully while Penga leaned closer, curiosity getting the better of her. The Dark One remained looming nearby in silence.“Okay,” she said. “Start with... ‘Zuko.’”Ho Tun froze mid-brush. Penga looked horrified.“Sifu, Toph” she whispered, “you can’t address the Fire Lord by just his name.”Toph tilted her head. “Sure I can.”Ho Tun hesitated before slowly writing the name.“Now write…” Toph grinned suddenly, sharp and mischievous.‘You owe me a field trip.’”

Far, far away from here, there was a party, there were people, there was his sister, her boyfriend, his best-friends and one too many strangers, all dancing together in a room.
Right here though, there was only him, and the guy he had almost kissed three hours ago. Him and the guy he had liked since he saw a picture. Him and the guy he took drawing classes with. “You don’t hate me then?” Sokka worded out, his voice balancing between a mix of playful, shy and absolutely liquefying with fear and anxiety.

He manages to hide himself against the lockers again, back sliding against the doors to squat on the floor. His back hits a lock. He cringes at the sound it makes, pressing his lips into a thin line to prevent himself from making any more noise. The sounds from the bench area stop. Oh shit oh shit oh shit—

He’s afraid to peek again, fearing that if he sees Zuko’s face, his assumption will be real. He squats on the floor, still unable to process what the fuck is happening.

A familiar burn sparked inside Jet's chest, and with it came a fury of realizations. Lee was never Lee. He was Zuko, the whispered-about banished prince of the Fire Nation, now Fire Lord. Jet had been right all along. He was an ashmaker, and he was a liar and a fraud.Zuko had long since settled into a solitary routine. His closest friends, spread across the world, only visited on occasion. Uncle Iroh had retired to his tea shop. Suki and Ty Lee left when he relieved the Kyoshi Warriors of their duty, when the assassination attempts died down, and he could hardly call any of his current ministers or guards 'friends.' While he and Mai stayed in touch, they were never as close as they once were. He had not set eyes on his sister in years.

title: Until The Sun Rises

“Come on, It was just a prank Mai-Mai!” Toph yells out to her.
Slowly, one by one, their smiles began to wear off. Mai had quickly disappeared from view after she bolted straight into the woods. Yue had stepped out into the back patio now, curious to know what was going on.
“What happened? What did you guys do to her?” she anxiously asks. Yue scans all of her friends’ facial expressions. They were all apprehensive, Aang had lowered down his camera — the red light no longer blinkering. “We just wanted to pull a small prank on Mai…we didn’t think she’d react this way. The smoke dissipates and–
Holy shit.
There are no–holy Tui and La’s left pec–there are no words that can even begin to describe the magnificent creature that jumps into the air.
It's beautiful, is what Sokka’s brain manages to offer, followed immediately by the more pressing realization that his brain is not currently offering literally anything else.
He’s never seen something like it. Its deep, reflective scales make the ground glow red, and its tail swishes in dangerous waves against the dirt from where it rests. Its wings unfurl slowly, hesitantly expanding with flawless grace, and nothing that Sokka has ever seen could compare. Not like the polarbear-dogs back at home or even Appa or Momo. Its eyes rake over them, and Sokka is suddenly, acutely aware that he is standing in front of something that could absolutely decide he is lunch.
Sokka’s mind has never connected to his mouth in situations involving potential death. And the longer the silence stretches, the louder his survival instincts beg him to do anything but stand there and take it like a man.
So really, you can’t blame him.

title: Fire and Still Water
author: Jellyfishsthings
summary:
The announcement came on a Tuesday, when the leaves turned the color of fire and you were reading and the tea had gone cold.
You married the Fire Lord on a Thursday in autumn. You wore fire lilies in your hair. Neither of you wanted it. Neither of you said so.
What followed was not a love story — not at first. It was two people in the same building, running a nation between them, learning the shape of each other's silences. It was a lamp left on in a corridor at an hour when the palace should have been dark. It was tea refilled without being asked. It was the slow, painstaking work of two people who had forgotten how to want things, remembering.
She carries a fire that burns white and a secret that could undo everything. He carries the weight of a nation and the particular loneliness of someone who has never been seen clearly.
This is the story of what happens when they finally look.

summary:
“I cannot believe, I’m doing this,” Lin grumbles, the words low and sharp as she crosses her arms over her chest, staring out at the endless stretch of ocean. She does not need this. She does not need spiritual retreats, or quiet getaways, or any of this foolishness designed to soothe fragile minds. She has a police force. She has a city to protect and clean of corruption. She has built her legacy with her own two hands, stone by stone, arrest by arrest. She did not claw her way up to where she is today just to be defined by her last name, or by who her mother was. She is Lin Beifong, and she made it here on her own merit, not by luck, not by favor, and certainly not by being soft.
“I cannot believe I actually agreed to this,” she mutters under her breath, jaw tight, as the boat finally glides toward the dock. Ember Island. The famous retreat of the Fire Nation. A place meant for peace, for relaxation, for forgetting the world’s burdens.  Lin Beifong has never felt further from Republic City than she does right now.

summary: Zuko grew up hearing about soulmates. It was the most comforting thing in the world to him. Even if Azula was awful, even if Father didn't love him, even if Mother was gone, there was someone out there in the world destined to love him for who he was no matter what.He should have known it wouldn't be that easy. He didn't even know he'd met his soulmate until the bond sickness started setting in. His soulmate had rejected him so thoroughly and so immediately that it had severed the bond between them, leaving the broken end to rot and poison Zuko until he dies.The only way to save him is for his soulmate to rescind their rejection and accept the bond. Maybe that's the universe telling him to stay down this time. summary:
Zuko yearns for Katara's forgiveness, says he'll do whatever it takes to earn it. His attempts to do so causes her to be in denial as she slowly falls in love with him. He's angry he betrayed her trust in Ba Sing Se, and he is basically near groveling as each attempt fails.
Meanwhile Katara is in utter rejection. Ever since the spirit oasis in the Northern Tribe, she's been having dreams of her crowned as Zuko's Fire Lady, and being beside him as his wife. How can she accept those visions of the future when the boy in front of her has hurt her so?
"I was the first one to trust you back in Ba Sing Se!" She yelled, chest heaving, "And you turned around and betrayed me! Betrayed all of us!" He reached out a hand to pull her close when she pulled away, turning to face the sea.
He sank to his knees, kneeling in the cliffs swaying grass. "Katara," he pleaded.
She turned and his self-loathing constricted like a vice around his chest as her eyes shone with unshed tears.
"I want.. I want your forgiveness Katara," he swore, "It's doesn't matter how long it takes, I've chased the avatar endlessly before. I'll show you just how sorry I am, and how much I regret hurting you."

summary:
Aang has vanished. Ozai fell by his hand. Toph is gone. What remains is Azula. She wears the crown of the world now. Zuko and Katara are somewhere in the architecture of her cruelty, imprisoned, removed from the map of things Sokka is allowed to hope for.
Only Sokka remains free. He hides, building a plan from whatever the wreckage has left him. Azula finds him. Azula always finds what she is looking for.
She does not kill him. That would be too simple, and Azula has never been simple. She keeps him close, leashed, orbiting her like a moon that has forgotten it once had its own gravity. Her strange, infuriating pet, who refuses to be broken in any way that satisfies her.
And now a rebellion stirs in the dark and it turns its eyes to Sokka, because he is the one who is near her.
This is a story about what survives the end of everything. About a woman who has spent her entire life being both the fire and the thing it burns, and a man stubborn enough, foolish enough, human enough, to refuse to become ash.

"Who's that?" Sokka follows her gaze to a boy slumped in an alley between two stores. From far away Katara can make out the boy's yellow and orange patched hoodie, as well as a beanie and some fluffy mess on his lap.
The boy looks so peaceful as he sleeps, he can't be any older than fifteen, and it takes Sokka's looming shadow to break Katara's gaze from his face. "Why do you think he's sleeping here?" She asks her brother, who just shrugs.
"Why don't you ask him? Surely it can't be that comfortable to sleep here."
Gently, Katara shakes the boy's shoulder. He wakes up with a stir, slowly blinking his eyes open to reveal gray that stares into Katara's. Staring into his eyes, Katara feels a pull towards him. After a brief second, the boy realizes where he is.
"Wanna go skateboarding with me?"

The boarding bell rang again. Final call. Sokka exhaled sharply through his nose. “Tui and La, I hate leaving you.” Slowly and painfully, he kissed Zuko’s forehead.
“I’ll come back before the monsoon ends,” he murmured.
“You said that last time.”
“And I was right.”
“You were twelve days late.”
“The ocean is large.”
Zuko’s hand tightened around his sleeve. Sokka smiled sadly.
Then, because he could never resist provoking him one final time, he murmured:
“And if one of your ministers suddenly falls down a staircase while I’m gone, I’ll know you missed me.”
That earned him the smallest laugh imaginable. He looked relieved to hear it. Then he stepped backward toward the ship.
At the top of the boarding ramp, he turned once more. Zuko remained standing exactly where he had left him, robes snapping violently in the sea wind.

“Goodnight, Sokka.”
He brushed past him toward the door. Their shoulders collided lightly as Zuko passed, and he caught how cold he felt through the thin rehearsal shirt. Sokka stayed there another moment, staring at his reflection of the room in the mirrors. Then he looked toward the speaker, the discarded water bottle, the untouched food sitting half-hidden inside Zuko’s bag pocket before the zipper had fallen shut.
And for reasons Sokka couldn’t explain yet, walking away from the studio felt much more difficult than it should have.—Zuko is the best dancer at Agna Qel Conservatory. He’s also exhausted, starving, and emotionally volatile. Sokka plays hockey, thinks ballet is ridiculous, and keeps accidentally running into Zuko while picking up his sister from rehearsals. Unfortunately, the more Sokka sees of the ballet world, the less he understands why someone would willingly destroy themselves for it.

"Well, I sort of lied before. We did meet once. In Ba Sing Se."
Zuko's eyes widen immediately. A knot in his brain finally untied. "The teashop."
"Yeah, and I haven't understood why until today but..." Jia's hands still, mind drifting from the dull throb along her arm, "I can't stop thinking about you."
He takes a sharp sort of inhale. "Look, I kind of just broke up with my girlfriend and—"
"What?" Jia recoils. "What's wrong with you?"
"Oh. I just thought—"
"Stop. Thinking." She turns back to the water. Her rippling reflection in the moonlight. "You have this look on your face. Like... like you don't know where to go."
She dips her hand back into the water. Lets the stream flow between her fingers. "And the others are right. You've done horrible things and you're the son of the Firelord, so I should hate you—and maybe I do!"
Then she thinks back to a time when she hated herself too. Giving in to all kinds of bad habits in the name of necessity. Crying at the walls of Ba Sing Se.
Maybe that self-hatred never went away.
"I know that look. I've worn it," she admits quietly. "I don't think it's something you can fake."

There are so very many things wrong with the Crown Princess of the Fire Nation. She does not think, speak, nor act in any way approaching normalcy and yet, as dictated by her position of supreme power, she cannot be ignored. If she was ever to fall, if her profound intelligence, skill, and authority were all to be bested, there is no doubt that the influence of her actions on those closest to her and so many more would make for scars that will never fade.

Stuck on a ship that can’t take her to where she wants to go and unable to return home, Kiyoi pleads with the kind old man that catches her stealing from the ship's pantry to take her in as a servant. summary:
The Fire Nation took your parents. Just like that. You became a ward of Gaoling's state, then a ward of Cai Bingwen, the most successful cabbage merchant in the middle market, who had bigger dreams than Gaoling could contain and a cart that needed pushing.So you pushed it. Across the Earth Kingdom, through every mid-tier town with a mid-tier inn. But you had a roof, a bowl of cabbage soup, and a place at Ba Sing Se University waiting for you at the end of it - because that was the deal you'd made with yourself at age seven. You were going to make something out of this.
And then Team Avatar happened.You watched them destroy everything. The cart. The cabbages.  You stood there and watched Cai sink to his knees in the dirt and wail, and something in you went very cold.
You were going to make them pay for that.
Fortunately, you weren't the only one. Somewhere out there was a banished prince with the worst ponytail you'd ever seen and enough repressed emotions to fuel a small war, who hated Team Avatar just as much as you did, possibly more. He was dramatic. He had issues. A lot of them.
But the enemy of your enemy was your friend.Even if your friend needed to seriously reconsider his hair.

There was a time when Zuko truly believed that he would never be happy. When capturing The Avatar and returning home seemed like an impossible feat. so when the war ended, the board simply reset.
To stabilize a fragile peace, she is forced into a political marriage with Fire Lord Zuko as a necessary sacrifice. Arriving not as a bride, but a pawn.

He knows what political marriages do to people, his mother was testament of that. But the colonies are fracturing, the peace is crumbling, and his advisors are watching.

but zuko seems to forget that on the board, only position matters.and she is already moving to the other side.

fandoms: Avatar: The Last Airbender: Chronicles of the Avatar Novels - Various
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary:
"Zuko."
"I lied."
Toph let out a soft, faint smile as she watched Zuko walk away without turning his head. She did not reach out to hold him back; she simply let herself lean into the exact spot where he had just been sitting. Her clouded eyes, filled with profound satisfaction, drifted shut. Perhaps she did not even notice that as her eyes closed, a tear traced a long path down her youthful cheek. Her consciousness gradually blurred under the arriving summer heat; her hands hung loose upon the bench where his hands had once rested, her lips still slightly curved with the overflowing happiness of having loved. Toph's face in this moment was peaceful to the point of aching, yet fulfilled to the point of heartbreak.
Under the summer sun, Toph departed from the mortal world with a love that had only just begun, yet was already severed.
Toph Beifong—had died ten years ago, by suicide.
Zuko—the one who had seen the ghost of the rumors.

summary:
Sokka has always liked the idea of meeting a mermaid. After all, for a sailor, the only thing better than the company of a woman (besides his sister) is that of a half-fish-half-woman who loves the sea as much as he does! Of course, after the Fire Nation sinks his ship, leaving him stranded in the waters of Blood Moon Bight, he’s not too interested in mingling with the local tribe of man-eating mermaids.
His chances of winding up a midnight mer-snack for a carnivorous fish-lady? Very high. His chances of being found by a mermaid with a pickier palate who keeps him as her prisoner and only promises to free him in exchange for information about the surface world because she hates subaquatic life and wants to leave the sea altogether? The smile fades and he takes a longer drag, letting smoke cloud over his face like a mirage.
“…Lot’s of things are bad for you.”
He adjusted his cuffs, showing off more pale forearm.
“But people indulge in them anyways.”
Sokka looked away pointedly.

summary:
Whenever he slept, the boy was there.
Dreammates shared dreams when they happened to both be asleep at the same time, of course. The elders said the tides of dreams were dangerous to sink into alone for some, and so the spirits gave them dreammates to keep their souls safe when sleeping. Like ottercats holding onto one another as they floated at sea.
Not everyone had such gifts, and most people only had one or two people to share dreams with. In their village, it was customary that if two children were dreammates that their parents put them down for naps together like family. After all, if the tides of dreams were dangerous, why let anyone go alone who didn’t have to?
Though, Sokka and Katara were never alone when they slept.
There were others who joined their dreams sometimes, three girls and another boy.
But the one boy was always, always, there.
And he never seemed to get any older.
---

title: The Mask and the Avatar - Book 1: Three Kings
author: Anonymous
summary:
Republic City is a city held together by compromise. Four triads keep the underworld balanced. A bending council keeps the government upright. A police force, outnumbered and outspent, keeps the peace where it can. It has worked, more or less, for seventy years.
Then the Terra Triad is massacred in a single night, and nobody knows who did it.
Korra arrives in the middle of a turf war she does not understand, to study airbending with Tenzin and find her place in a city that has never needed an Avatar before. The triads are carving up the ruins of their fourth rival. The council is deadlocked. The papers are full of a masked man who executes criminals in public and walks away before the police arrive, and the nonbenders of the working districts are starting to cheer for him.
His name is Amon. He preaches equality. He calls bending a sickness. He is patient, and disciplined, and far more dangerous than the triads he hunts.
By the time Korra understands what he actually wants, he will already have done half of it.

title: Korra: The Legend Retold
author: Tree_The_Pretentious
summary:
I love Korra. She's amazing, she's hot, she was indisputably my transbian awakening. It was a great story and a fantastic continuation of the greatest show of all time. But I know I'm not the first person to say there are some flaws in the writing. And the plot. And the characters. And the themes.
My goal is to rewrite Season 1 with my own spin on it, divided into 3 seasons to give more room to explore the characters, as well as the nuances of the equalist movement. Korra will be treated with more dignity, not portrayed as a petulant child who breaks things when she's angry but as a fledgling avatar; a flawed character who's forced to learn and grow as she experiences her newfound freedom. Mako, Bolin and Asami will all have deliberate arcs, and nonbender oppression will be portrayed and contemplated both directly and indirectly. The equalist movement itself will be more complex, with multiple leaders, and Amon will not be the sole face of it. Everything will have more time to dive into the nuance that the writers had to leave on the cutting room floor. And goddamnit, why does Korra lose so many fights?
I may continue this past season one if the impulse strikes me as well. But for now, I hope you enjoy!

Transformed into the spirit of the moon, she watched silently over the world, guiding heroes from afar, comforting those in need, and finding solace in the stories of a distant, tragic, and brilliant world called Middle-earth.
But her story does not end in the quiet of moonlight. Fate has plans beyond the celestial realm. She is reborn as the only daughter of Maedhros, the eldest of the sons of Fëanor, in a family steeped in fire, brilliance, and tragedy. Already aware of their history, she navigates a world where her presence is unprecedented, her identity a mystery, and her mission unspoken: to help her father find redemption and to carry forward the light of both her past and her new lineage.
In this tale, Isilmë must reconcile two worlds, the mortal and the immortal, the Water Tribe and the House of Fëanor, and discover the power of love, sacrifice, and hope.

Hakoda, chief of the Southern Water Tribe, has three children. He adores each of them, even though they confuse him at times. Katara, his youngest, was born early on a cool morning - he remembers that the waters seemed oddly vibrant that day. She grew in to a strong-willed young woman with a talent for waterbending, despite never having a teacher.
Sokka, the second-born, was born at noon in a cold day that seemed far too normal. Clouds dotted the sky like they'd been meticulously placed and the waves crashed into the ice precisely every five seconds. Sokka grew to be a clever boy. Though he couldn't bend, he had a mind that challenged those of the boys twice his age.
Finally Hakoda's oldest - the one that confused him the most. He was born at midnight under a full moon so large, it looked like it would have touched the ground. In the quiet between fire's shadow and water's truth, a life shaped by survival begins to reveal itself.
Giyuu Tomioka has always walked between worlds — first as a child who arrived where they did not belong, and later as someone who learned to survive by becoming quiet enough to be overlooked. They grow up in a land that never quite understands them, a place where silence becomes a shield and gentleness becomes a kind of armour.
As he grows older, Giyuu is drawn into conflicts far larger than himself, surrounded by people who mistake his quiet for coldness and his distance for indifference. He becomes a steady presence in a world that keeps shifting beneath his feet, a constant in the lives of those who rarely see him clearly.
Yet even the softest lives can shape the world around them. And even those who pass unnoticed leave echoes that linger long after their footsteps fade.
This is the story of someone who was never fully understood, and the quiet mark she leaves on a world that only learned her name when it was too late.

Zuko popped another spoonful of rice into his mouth and chewed it slowly, relishing the slight sweetness. He swallowed and sighed. “The first meeting starts at noon. “Aw,” Sokka pouted. “But I like yelling!”
Zuko huffed a laugh and reached for the teapot again. “Don’t you dare start another war.”
“No promises.”
Zuko picked the grain of rice off his forehead and flicked it back.

summary:
A journey documenting Zuko's redemption and his developing relationship with Sokka as he struggles to manage his Blue Spirit identity.
Zuko desperately missed the scorching weather in the Fire Nation. He distantly remembered sitting by the water with his mother, feeding the turtleducks, the sun beaming down on his face. It was a warmth that enveloped him, gentle, not scorching. It made him feel connected to the ancient source of their power. Like Agni itself was shining down on him.
Even as he grew older and had less of a place, much less a person, to call home, his respite would come from the sun’s gentle light.
The Earth Kingdom was milder, although it felt more stuffy. The air did not carry the subtle scent of smoke and blooming Fire Lilies. He could never feel truly comfortable here, surrounded by the menacing walls of Ba Sing Sae.
He felt like a caged bird, one that had never really known true freedom.
Basically, Zuko joins the Gaang earlier, but still has to deal with his conflicting feelings. Sokka is completely enamoured with the elusive Blue Spirit.Tags will be updated!

"Wait..."

Instead, as he had done so many, too many times before, he said nothing. Bryce was right to laugh at him. He was such a coward.
 
"Dad?"
"Yes, Terry...let's go..."
 
Clark saw him turn away, his body doing nothing, his voice caught in his throat.
It was Dick who took action.
"We're here for you."
"I already said I'm not enlisting..."
"You're the Avatar!"

He failed. The war was supposed to end on the Day of the Black Sun… but he failed. He failed his friends, his team, everyone, and the whole world.
Sleep never comes, his thoughts keep him awake as the weight of his failure bears down on him, suffocating even within the Western Air Temple’s refuge. And when he finds himself on the shores below the temple one night, desperate for air and silence, something pulls him from his melancholy.
A rowboat. Out here?
Were they discovered? Tracked? Who would end up aground in a place like this?
-----
She tried to kill him once, and for a moment, she did.
Unlike her pathetic brother, she was always smarter, more cunning, the prodigal child their father wanted. And yet, even after her nation’s victory on the Day of the Black Sun, the Crown Princess is broken, clinging to life by sheer will and the skin of her teeth.
The last thing she remembers is reaching shore… somewhere… escaping that bastard Earth Kingdom general’s stronghold with everything she had left.
Far from her fleet, far from her subordinates, she knows her chances of survival are slim.
Still, a small part of her prays, hopes even, that maybe, just maybe…

summary:
But then why is he chasing you? A voice in the back of his mind spoke up. Why isn’t he back at the Royal Palace, doing… royalty stuff? Aang was fairly sure there hadn’t been any runaway princes a hundred years ago – at least not without an army to back them up. And he was trying, he really was, but Zhao was scary and Zuko was technically a traitor, and were you still even royalty if you betrayed the Fire Lord–?
Looking back at Zuko, Aang made his choice.
And saw that it was much, much too late for that choice to mean anything.
––
Aang takes a little too long to act when he discovers the Blue Spirit’s identity — an identity soon exposed at large — and Zuko is brought back to Pohuai Stronghold. That night, Aang overhears a little too much, and Zuko gains a little too good of an understanding of what it means to be captured. With chances of returning home dwindling, Zuko is forced to consider his options, while Aang is ecstatic that there may be more to Zuko’s motivations than they all thought.
All the while, a letter is racing over the seas to the Royal Palace. And one Fire Nation Princess may soon be on everyone’s trail…
(Or: An exploration of the butterfly effect.)

After the war, Zuko rules a nation in recovery.
By day, that means meetings, decrees, decisions. It means being the king everyone expects him to be. It means moving forward, rebuilding, leaving the fire behind.
But night is another matter.
When the palace falls silent. When the reports are signed and the advisors have left. When there is nothing and no one left to demand his attention, and therefore, nothing to distract him from the one thing that is always there, lurking in the depths of his mind.
Then, his feet move on their own.
It's not a decision. It's not a duty.
Always to the same place.
Always to the same door.

summary:
"Life happens wherever you are, whether you make it or not." -Uncle Iroh'~.~'--'~.~'
On the ferry, Jet thought he'd found a kindred spirit.
Zuko had the good sense to be wary of making friends in the city.
It was a passing fascination with one another that had ended the moment Jet spotted previously cold tea steaming in a cup.In another world, an evenly-matched fight in the street and an arrest by the Dai Li would be the final time their paths would ever cross.
This, however, was not that world.Somehow, someway, the strings of fate had unwound and rewoven to give their story a different ending.
Beneath the waters of Lake Laogai, the rocks sent Jet's way did not land a fatal blow.
Beneath the palace of Ba Sing Se, Zuko made a different choice.

✅Book 1

Sometime during 2020 I discovered an infamous series of online comics, showing this strange, Twilight Zone universe, one in which Sokka and Katara are fighting for an evil Water Tribe whilst Aang is travelling the world with a good Azula and Zuko. Reading a few chapters of the fanfiction it was based on, I quickly discovered a message from the author Ogro/Baithin, who apparently abandoned the fic and gave his blessings for others to do with the premise whatever they wanted.
I set out to create a remake, one with a structure that more closely resembles ATLA’s TV show format. On the verge of uploading my first chapter, I found out the original Distorted Reality had been continued. Encouraged by Ogro himself, I went ahead with my version of the story anyway.
I originally uploaded the first chapter on 2/1/2021 on fanfiction.net. It has since grown to an enormous size, and I’m enormously happy with how it’s turning out with time, both as an ATLA fanfic, as a reimagining of DR, and as just my own little story and universe.
Just take your time with it. It's a long one.
Enjoy!

summary: A very reluctant Avatar:One of the male sages cleared his throat to speak up, "We are the Fire Nation's Sages, and we've been tasked with a matter of the utmost importance: finding the next Avatar."Vi let out a snorted laugh. "Okay? Well, you're in the wrong place."The woman stepped forward. She was rather young, especially compared to the older, grey haired men. She confidently stated, "I don't believe we are."As she ended her sentence, she planted her foot and extended a balled fist toward Vi. A line of fire shot out toward the redhead.Without thinking, Vi swirled her hands before her in a circular motion, creating an air shield, and pushed them outward to disperse the fire.The room went silent as the fire disappeared and the wind from the conjured air stilled. Vi returned her hands to rest on her knees and her eyes were wide at her own mistake."Fuck," she whispered.Golden eyes shimmered, and a smile crept onto the woman's lips. “My name is kind of weird, too, you know.” The other girl sat down in the grass beside her. It was reflex that Deki turned away slightly to shield her ink painting, but the other girl didn’t seem to notice.

Warm, unfamiliar and— she’d imagine this was what others felt when they came home to someone and ate dinner together. Something like home. title: The Fire Burns You Away

summary:
There is a story told in the Fire Nation, passed from the Fire Sages to their children, that the brightest stars in the sky are cousins of Agni—spirits who wandered into the dark so they might forever share their light when he rests. Some say they are spirits even more powerful than Agni himself. Others recount tales of exile, claiming they were cast from his side for being too volatile to remain in the world.
But all Fire Sages agree on two things.
The brightest stars die faster than the rest.
And every one of them burns a deep, furious blue.
When Azula is born, the stars themselves weep for her.

summary:
What is the limit of bending? How far can it go?
Two sides — which one will prevail? Those who wish to conquer, or those who fight to survive?
Regardless of the victor, what will be left to rule if the world is in ashes?
Or
A hundred years ago, when the Fire Nation exterminated the four Air Temples and ruthlessly hunted down the surviving Nomads, they never imagined that, months before the massacre, a man would give up everything it meant to be an Air Nomad — renouncing his culture, his faith, and even his bending, in search of a common life in the Earth Kingdom.
Thanks to that choice, eighty-three years later, an airbender unlike any other would be born. He would not hide, nor would he follow the pacifist ideals of his ancestors. On the contrary: he would bend air in the most lethal way possible — without limits, without restraint.
He would become a scourge, determined to end the war and, above all, to kill the Fire Nation's royal family.

title: Jade & Jasmine
author: importantstudentbusinessspyblog
summary:
“Welcome to the Fire Nation,” I say flatly. “I suppose this will be your new home. Though I wouldn’t get comfortable if I were you. I am not interested in concubines at the moment.”
Gasps echo down the line. Hands fly to mouths. The sound scraping against my nerves.
I move on. “You will be confined to the palace walls. Guarded by eunuchs wherever you go.”
Then I add a bite to my tone. “And should I hear any trouble… There will be severe punishment.”
The words taste like ash. They sound like him. I force myself to meet their eyes so they know I mean it. “This will be a harem in appearance only. I am far too-”
And then I see her. The words die.
Her gown is the colour of pine, patterned in threads of gold. It clings, then falls, loose trousers underneath. A jade pin glints in her black hair. My mouth goes dry. Jin.
The girl I remember as sweet and soft and has been carved into something sharp. Her cheekbones hollower; her jaw an elegant line. Her eyes, distrusting and yet familiar and dark green, catch mine and widen. Surprise flickers across her face, turning to recognition, then something else. Her lips part.
And I almost imagine the whisper of a name I hadn't heard in years. 'Lee?'

title: Zuko Never Liked the Cold

summary:
"Sokka" Zuko spoke, garnering the tribesman's attention.
"Fire Lord Zuko," Sokka said, lowering his gaze to avoid Zuko's eyes, "you look well," Zuko felt so small.
Sokka spoke mechanically, rehearsed, like the conversation was strained and the six words were something he might choke on.
It dawned on him.
Zuko was alone, not even Hakoda was here to defend him from the carnivorous harpies, it was just him.  His hands shook, lips trembled, but he did his best to show face.  His smile disappeared, his warmth dying like the last coals on a hearth, and Zuko felt cold.
He hated the cold.

After Oboro's heartfelt exit, Midnight is in shambles; she can’t stop thinking about her.
“Can a villain be redeemed? Especially when they are so one-dimensionally evil and simple?” Midnight asks.
Oboro was never written to be anything more than a pervy villain. All she knows is cruelty and domination, but there is more to lust than just domination and power. There is also submission and trust—a lesson Midnight wants oh so badly to teach her.
In this multiverse-hopping adventure, Midnight, with the help of her friends, plans a redemption arc, hires a villain to play “the heavy,” and redeems a once one-note villain for the whole multiverse to see.

title: My Avatar Academia
author: JJGSkywalker
fandoms: 僕のヒーローアカデミア | Boku no Hero Academia | My Hero Academia (Anime & Manga)
summary: What if the Avatar world was spun into My Hero Academia? Four nations of people, connected by the consistency of elemental quirks, once with great influence, that over the centuries, shrank. What if there was a reincarnating quirk, one that balanced these four groups, whose most recent five incarnations fought alongside the user of the quirk passed down through generations? What if Zuko, Katara, Toph, Sokka, and Aang went to UA? What if Izuku Midoriya was in Class 1-B?This isn’t just a “What if we did a funky Avatar and MHA Crossover?” This is fundamentally a reimagining of My Hero Academia in many ways, with more than enough references, callbacks, and frankly shoehorns of other popular media into this universe of heroes and quirks, as well as it's share of oriignal characters. It’s a self-indulgent fanfic that I’m not even sure I’ll fully commit to, nor can I promise it will be good. But I want to write, and this concept, born from endless My Hero Academia roleplays with one of my best friends, is something I want to do. Read at your own risk, especially if you cringe easily. So without further ado. Let us embark, welcome one and all, to your hero academia.

title: Hakoda Adopting a Broken Fire Prince: Avatar the Last Airbender
author: Cryztaliz
summary:
Long after the camp has fallen silent, Zuko wakes from a restless sleep and slips away from the others. He puts distance between himself and the group, choosing the cold and darkness to face what he believes he must endure alone. His body betrays him pain, exhaustion, and the consequences of wounds long ignored begin to take their toll. The prince breaks quietly, unseen, far from the warmth of the fire.Some time later, Hakoda wakes.At first, it is nothing more than instinct, a sense that something is wrong. When he notices Zuko's absence, unease settles in. Against reason, against the history written in war and blood, Hakoda rises and goes searching.He finds Zuko at his worst.Not as the Fire Nation's prince. Not as an enemy.
But as a suffering child, shaking, failing, and desperately trying to hold himself together.As Zuko's condition worsens and his strength fades, Hakoda makes a choice that defies everything the world has taught him. He stays. He steadies trembling hands. He offers comfort where none was expected. In that moment, Hakoda becomes more than a leader of the Southern Water Tribe, he becomes a father figure to a boy who has never truly had one.

Reborn into a world torn by the Hundred Year War, Tai Lung, the fallen warrior of the Jade Palace, is adrift in a new life. Haunted by the memories of his past failures and the teachings of Master Shifu, he now travels the world burdened by doubt.

title: The Polar Prisoners
author: ErsatzErmine
summary: He opened his mouth to reassure his uncle, to tell him that he’d be able to start running in just as second, just as soon as the world stopped spinning, but instead all he muttered was, “I’m tired.”When Iroh brushed against the back of Zuko’s head the pain there abruptly muscled to the front of Zuko’s list of issues, and he gave a loud groan. Iroh pulled back quickly, but Zuko could see that his hand was now dripping with blood.“Then you should rest, Prince Zuko,” Iroh said, his voice calm and controlled, which would’ve been very nice if the lines of concern on his face hadn’t been so obvious. Zuko watched blearily as Iroh began to look sharply around them, apparently assessing something. “A man needs his rest.”The world started getting hazy again, but the lack of attempted movement was a slight improvement. A series of shouts pulled him back from the creeping numbness, and Zuko forced his eyelids open.Iroh was waving his arms, signaling to someone. “We surrender!” Iroh bellowed. “I am with the Crown Prince of the Fire Nation, and he needs a doctor!”***OR:Zuko and Iroh are taken prisoner by the Northern Water Tribe following the battle in Agna Qel’a.

But it wasn’t enough time. Zuko knew the Avatar and his friends were strong. They were courageous enough to take on the challenge of saving the world! But would it be enough?

summary:
After years spent rebuilding the world—and somehow surviving the bureaucratic nightmare that is early Republic City—Zuko decides everyone deserves a break. His solution: a summer getaway on Ember Island, complete with sunshine, ocean breezes, and absolutely no chance of emotional catastrophe. Allegedly.Sokka is… less convinced. His ex‑girlfriend will be there, blissfully in love with her new girlfriend. Which is fine. Totally fine. He’s mature. He’s evolved.
But that’s not the real problem.
The real problem is the island itself—the place where he and Zuko once shared a moment so intimate and confusing that both of them tried to forget it.
And Ember Island has a reputation. It peels people open. It forces truth to the surface. It has a way of turning “we don’t talk about that” into “we really need to talk about that.”
So what happens when Sokka is trapped on a beach with his ex, his feelings, and the Firelord he maybe‑sort‑of‑accidentally kissed?
Ember Island always reveals the heart. Sokka just isn’t sure he’s ready for his to be seen.

Zuko does what he’s always done; he keeps going. There isn’t much of a choice for someone who was lucky to be born — you really can’t do anything unless you’re prepared to do it against the odds. There would come a time after the fight, grueling work rewarded by rest and recognition. An end, or at least a respite, or an upturn of some sort. He still clung desperately to that idea. Losing sight of it felt like death.

summary: After the war, the world builds nurseries.On a small volcanic island in the eastern sea—officially a “restricted zone,” unofficially called Shidō, the Island of First Steps—the White Lotus and the new nations hide something precious: a quiet village where tiny fire, earth, and waterbenders learn how not to fear themselves.Logan has been there three years.   “Your uncle tried to accompany you, but the Fire Lord has decreed that he is too useful to the nation as a General and has reinstated his position. He has not been allowed to see you.” The voice sounded hurried and urgent. “They are not allowing me to come on the journey and tend to your injury either.”
  Zuko was injured. His father had burned his face. He was banished, he was injured, and he was close to death. But Zuko was sure of at least one thing: He would survive. He had to. He was going to capture the Avatar and regain his honour. This was his last thought before he slipped into unconsciousness. A promise to himself and his nation.
When Zuko loses the Agni Kai he is branded as a traitor to his nation and banished. The Fire Lord decrees general Iroh too valuable to be allowed to accompany his disgraced nephew. He is abandoned instead - left to fend for himself in a fire nation colony.

“Your father and your uncle, they fight.  They don’t always get along.  But you two, my Zuko and Azula, you are the light of the Fire Nation.”  Ursa squeezes their shoulders gently.  “When your uncle is Fire Lord, and your cousin Lu Ten is next in line, you will be important players in the royal court.  There will be people who will try to divide you.  You Must Not Let Them.” She emphasizes every word, looking at them seriously.  “You are siblings, and you love each other.  Promise me that you’ll always look out for each other.”

“I promise,” Azula says.

title: Need and Want
author: meowrina
tags: after we get through all the angst first
summary:
“I needed you to stay with me back then. I needed you, somebody I could cry to, who wouldn’t think of me as somebody weak for shedding tears. I needed you to fight by my side when assassins wanted my head every other week. I needed you to laugh next to me and make me think that even if the world is shitty, at least you brought happiness to me. I needed you as a friend and as a partner…” he said and his voice started going softer, “And I wanted you to stay, because you were the woman I loved.” 
Gone was the prince who showed her awkward but affectionate smiles, and what stood in front of her was a Fire Lord hardened by years on the throne. Zuko was a shell of his former self, now formal and cold. For once, Katara threw away what she needed to do and instead followed her heart to get what she wanted.

After a century of war, Zuko knows peace isn’t built from treaties alone. It’s carved from guilt, blood, and the quiet terror of wondering if he’ll ever be more than his father’s son. As he joins Aang and the rest of the gang in Republic City, Zuko carries the weight of a nation’s sins on his shoulders and the fear that no matter how many homes he helps build, his scar will always define him.
Set against the fragile years after the war and the uncertain birth of Republic City, Zuko and Katara find themselves navigating love, loyalty, and leadership while the world struggles to heal. He wrestles with the burdens of the Fire Lord’s throne, fearful of binding Katara to a crown that could cage her. She seeks to support him without losing herself, even as grief, political tensions, and sacrifice test her strength.
It is during this period of change that they grow closer. Together, they face not only external threats to peace but also the internal battles of trust, vulnerability, and the fear of losing each other. Through moments of quiet tenderness and devastating honesty, they begin to realize that love is both a sanctuary and a crucible. One that shapes them into who they are meant to become.

summary:
A Foreword by the Scholar Zuyen:
It has been a long upheld truth of our great nation that after the twin falls of the disgraced Fire Lord Ozai and Princess Azula, and their subsequent imprisonments, neither of the two ever regained contact with our well-respected Fire Lord Zuko. While Fire Lord Zuko ensured the humane holding conditions of his estranged father and sister immediately after his ascension to the throne, he reportedly never saw a need to continue communications with them. Before writing this book, my answer to such an obvious statement would have been, "Blasting flames—well of course he didn't!" Now, though, my answer would be quite different. But best leave that til later.
Fire Lord Zuko, when questioned about such matters, only ever gave one answer in response, saying: “A true leader has no need for snakes and scoundrels. Dragons are far superior.”
Given his far more professional reply, it is no wonder that he was the fire lord and I am a less-than-humble scholar.

Her body remained angled away from them. She hadn’t decided whether to kill them yet. It would’ve been easy—too easy. A twist of her wrist, a flick of metal, and they’d be off Derpy’s back and falling through the clouds. But her muscles trembled from exhaustion, and she could taste the iron of her own blood in the back of her throat. She hated that. She hated being tired.
Still, she hated company more.
Taller girl spoke next. Her tone was clipped and cold, the sound of someone used to command. “Mira Jin.”
“Zoey Myung,” the smaller girl followed softly, hesitant but firm.
“So, you are the princess,” Rumi said bluntly, her voice cutting through the wind.
Zoey blinked, startled. “Uh, yeah…? Wait—how do you—are you blind? Sorry, that might be insensitive.”
“No.” Rumi’s tone didn’t change. One word, perfectly balanced between irritation and indifference.
Mira’s gaze hardened. “You’re debating killing us.”
“Correct.” The word was almost whispered, like it was obvious.

title: the heart is a lonely hunter (i know i've sinned, take me back to your loving arms)
author: insomniacscribbles
tags: Kyoshi is unaware of her rizz
summary:
The control Rangi tried to hold herself with had finally stretched thin. Maybe it was just having to sit around so much helplessly. Maybe it was the audacity of this girl to show up out of nowhere and confuse everything. But she had enough. “This is beyond your pride,” she hissed, her arm moving in a blur of a familiar motion. The cold, blue steel of her revolver was pinned against Kyoshi’s chest now.
Whereas any normal person would have jolted or flinched, she stayed eerily still. Unnerving. Is she an idiot? The metallic click of the hammer being drawn back was obscenely loud in the quiet. “You’re a variable I can not control. A mere distraction.”
The accusation hung heavy between them, but fear was the last thing in Kyoshi’s eyes. Fiercely, – stupidly – determined, she was.
“Am I?” she whispered, her own hand rising not to bat the weapon away, but to clasp it, her fingers wrapping around the barrel, holding it fast against her ribcage. “Or are you afraid, Deputy, of having a witness to whatever you become out there?”

summary: “How many catowls do you have to see to think it’s strange? Before you’d notice something was wrong?”It had taken Zuko all of two seconds to come up with his answer, a scowl on his face and fists clenched at his sides.“One. Catowls aren’t native to the Fire Nation: only the Earth Kingdom.”In the moment, Zuko was so sure and so strong-willed that it only made sense. But he was wrong.The answer was three catowls. The first wouldn’t seem real. After all, he’d never seen it before, so it was probably a fluke. The second would be real, sure, but he’d assume that would be the first catowl, and would think that maybe it was migrating. The third catowl would finally tip him over the edge. title: Ashes of a Forgotten Flame
author: Pokemook530
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary:
When Avatar Aang defeats Fire Lord Ozai in their fated final battle, he calls upon the ancient art of energybending to strip Ozai of his firebending. But in the chaos of spiritual forces colliding, Aang’s power goes too far. Along with Ozai’s bending, he takes something far deeper—his memory.
Now, the once-tyrannical Phoenix King awakens with no recollection of his crimes, his empire, or even his own name. He remembers nothing of hate or pride, only confusion and fear. To the world, he is the monster who nearly burned it to ash. To himself, he is a hollow shell seeking to understand who he used to be.
As the Fire Nation rebuilds, Zuko is torn between justice and mercy—should he imprison a man who no longer exists, or forgive a father who cannot remember his sins? Katara questions the morality of Aang’s choice, fearing that his compassion may have rewritten the balance between punishment and redemption. Toph and Sokka debate the meaning of accountability in a world seeking peace. And Aang himself must confront what it truly means to restore balance—if erasing a soul’s darkness is an act of mercy, or of hubris.

Nothing made sense around Mirabel, not since she was five years old. In a family of extraordinary people, she was normal, out of place, the odd one out.But, in the past few years, she’d started scampering off with Dolores for extended periods of time. Yukio’s things were moved out of the attic and hidden in Dolores’ room. Water fell out of standing glasses, gusts of air surrounded her when she was angry or fearful, and sometimes the ground moved under her feet while she ran to and fro. Kaz has two real talents: firebending and getting herself into spectacularly bad situations.

tags: Toph Beifong and Zuko are Siblings
summary:
His thumb grazed the skin of her forearm, just  below her elbow .
The shock was electric. It wasn't pain; it was simply feeling—a sensation so overwhelming it threatened to buckle his knees. The warmth, the softness of the skin, the simple, undeniable reality of another human being resting against him.
He hadn't been touched like this since he was a child, before the Agni Kai, before the scar. He had forgotten what it felt like to be near someone whose intent was not to harm, command, or manipulate.
His breath hitched again, shallow and tight.
Toph stirred then. Not in fear, but recognition. As an earthbender, she was attuned to vibrations, to the shifts in a person's core. She didn't need eyes to see the sudden, desperate tremor that ran the length of his arms.
"Hey, Sparky," she whispered, her voice low. "You good?"
The question was gentle, devoid of mockery. It was worse than an insult.

author: Grapesshouldbecrunchy
tags: Azula and Zuko Have a Good Relationship (Avatar)
summary:
He’s gone.
“He’s weak,” Azula whispered, testing the sound. Her throat was tight. “He always was.”
Drip. Drip.
The shadow deepened, taking form. It didn’t look like Zuko as he was now—scarred, sullen, and righteous. It looked like the boy she used to torment: younger, angrier, constantly nursing a bruise, the topknot slightly askew.
He was standing right where the door should have been. He wasn't crying, but his eyes were wide and accusatory.
The atmosphere clamped down, pulling the metallic scent of dawn inward.
“You left,” Azula stated, her voice sharp, trying to pierce the illusion. “You chose them. You chose failure.”
The hallucination of Zuko didn’t move, but a whisper, dry and wounded, filled the space above the water drip. “I chose freedom. You chose chains.”
“I chose the throne!” she snapped, pushing herself off the cot. Her muscles screamed in protest, but she ignored them, sneering. “I chose victory. You will be hunted, Zuzu! You will be forgotten!”
“I’m not the one who’s alone, Azula.”
Day 3- hallucinations

title: Birthrights Unleashed

summary:
A caged tiger monkey.
This was a jail, no matter how much her jailers, brother, Aang, or anyone else tried to deny it. And if they treated her like an animal, she might as well act like one. This morning she didn't have the fire in her belly for that. Not yet. But maybe after a meal.
She dragged the tray across the floor and sat cross-legged in front of it, eating in stoic silence. She wished she had a chair. A princess would have a chair. A person would. But she had burnt hers. Her eyes flickered to the scorch marks along the walls, the blackened metal door frame and hinges.
They were scared of her.
Good. Let them be afraid.All Azula would need to escape is a helpful hand from an unlikely source. Someone, perhaps, who saw her true potential.

relationships: Aang & Toph Beifong & Katara & Sokka & Suki & Zuko
summary:
Ursa goes into labor on a cold, moonless night. A storm rages outside, and the air feels alive with lightning. Her labor lasts two days, and when she looks down at her baby, her heart stops. He’s deathly pale and as silent as the grave. His eyes are terrifyingly bright, a pale yellow-green only found in lightning, and his hair is as white as ash.
Four years later, her second child is born. Her labor is just as long, the storm just as wild, and this baby is born with the same white hair and electric eyes, this time a chilling blue.
Neither of them seem human.
Half a world away and ten years later, Kya prays desperately to Tui and La with her last breath. They respond in the most unusual of ways.
In the aftermath of the raid, Katara's eyes turn pure white, and she never sleeps. She watches the stars, singing old, old songs that are only half remembered. Sokka spends more and more time out on the ocean, and swears he can talk to the sea life. It's only a mild shock when they both begin growing gills.
Half a world away from that, Toph runs away for the first time, and finds that she's much stronger than anyone gives her credit for. Much, much stronger.

It was quiet, lonely and boring there. Aang couldn’t tell where he was or for how long he’s been there. He could hear whispers every now and then—voices of people he could vaguely remember though the faces never quite sprang to his mind. Male voices, female voices—all of them whispering in his head, telling him to hang on tight, just wait, he would get out of there eventually.
An eternity later he finally heard something different—the sound of a baby wailing, voice strong yet fresh, raw in a way only newly born babies could achieve. The flicker of an image crossed his mind—of a baby girl with barely any hair on her head. Her eyes were screwed shut as she cried, bundled up in warm, blue furs. A tired and happy woman’s voice exhaled the name Katara reverently.

title: if it’s messy then you know it’s really love
author: butterflia
tags: Song: Kiss and Make Up (Dua Lipa & BLACKPINK)
Song: I know it won't work (Gracie Abrams)
summary:
Sometimes love can be messy, non-linear, and complicated.Sometimes that makes us run from it; sprinting away from the other’s desertion of you.Sometimes you poke and prod, spewing triggers, knowing precisely how to cage your heart; making the ones who want hell and all of your worst just want you more.But, sometimes the fight we go through in order to keep that love, means it’s worth it. It means it’s enough.
And sometimes your ex-situationship shows up at your doorstep, following a half-year hiatus. So when you instinctively fight and fly, running for the hills while screaming “I hate you,” it’s met with further unyielding opposition.
-
“Love isn’t keeping people at bay, just to wash them up on shore when they dipped their toes in. It’s inviting people to swim with you, whether they drown you or keep you afloat. That gamble is what love is about.”
“I shouldn’t have to ask you to stay!”“Well, it doesn’t seem like you want me to stay. You hate me for leaving, so I come back, and you still hate me.”“How else am I supposed to feel about you leaving? Because unless your love language is being absent, then I would say my hatred is justified.”“So you do hate me?”“Yes!”

summary: In a world where the Avatar was killed during the airbender genocide, the cycle has been repeating for one hundred years. Each time, the Avatar is hunted and murdered by the tyrannical Fire Lord who has expanded his reign to most of the world and declared himself Emperor.Katara thought she was someone with unbreakable hope, but this world—this place—its devoured her. Surrounded by her enemy on every side, she has no one to turn to. Her home is hundreds of miles away, and she's been forced to live as a prisoner. The only thing keeping her alive is her ability to heal. The Fire Lord uses her to fix his wounded soldiers, and then she returns to the darkness of her cell. It's been seven years since she last saw the snow in the South Pole. Seven years since she's seen her brother. With no one to train her true power, she feels helpless. She's only ever around water to heal—she's not a fighter. She has no way out.Until she sees him again. The boy with the scar—she saved his life when she was twelve. It was how they discovered her abilities. And he may be the one to finally restore her hope. He may be her way out. If only she hadn't gone and fallen in love with him along the way.

summary: Who’s there?” a boy’s voice broke her thoughts.Snapping back to reality, Mai squinted at the dark figure moving near the pond. Something in his voice, his silhouette, felt familiar. Suddenly, a flame flickered to life in his palm, and she immediately knew who it was.“Z… Zuko?” she blurted, unable to hide her surprise. She hadn’t expected such a coincidence.The boy holding the flame slowly approached. As the firelight revealed her face, his stomach churned strangely. Her delicate features, pale skin, and sharp eyes, he suddenly new who she was.“Mai!?” Zuko exclaimed, startled, nervously taking a half-step back. “What are you doing here?”“Escaping your father’s boring banquet. You?” she replied flatly, avoiding his gaze.Or...Ozai threw a banquet to celebrate his coronation, and Mai couldn't put up with it. So she sneaked out of it. The girl just wanted to sit peacefully by the pond in the royal garden. Long ago, the gods who ruled the elements bickered and fought amongst themselves, until the Phoenix King asserted himself as supreme ruler. He was a flame deity, and as such, was more temperamental than most of the other gods. But he had an iron fist when it came to their rule, and he divided all those under him into the four elements.
 
  But this is not their story.

  A young godling once came into the court of the Sun God. He was ordered to shine brightly and bring draught to a village that the young god protected, but the young god disobeyed. In anger for acting against the Phoenix King, the young god was thrown from the Realm of the Gods into the World of Man. He was told to live among the mortals and learn his lessons in their world.

There were two kinds of crew, Zuko learned quickly. Those who were indifferent to him, and those who seemed to be very aware of who he was.
 
  It was best to stick around the first kind, the men and women Captain Jee brought aboard. They were gruff, and kept to themselves, and played incomprehensible games with coin and dice.

summary: After the battle at the Northern Water Tribe, Sokka is captured by Zhao.It's not incredibly ideal, however, he reckoned he could escape if given the right motivation. Most of which is provided by his cellmate, Prince Zuko, the boy they've been fearing for months. Sokka believed all Fire Nation was evil, that it was only capable to destroy. All he saw when he looked at the Fire Nation was the fire in their eyes. “These are feelings you might want, Katara,” he said, voice low, warm, dangerous in its honesty. “Please… don’t give up on them just yet.”

“Do you know how long I’ve waited to hear that?” he asked, voice barely a whisper. “How many nights I stayed awake thinking about that time we had… before you left?”

summary:
Kuai Liang swung his arms, ready to continue fighting, when something strange caught his attention. A gaze, sharp and attentive, seemed to pierce the back of his head. He turned and locked eyes with the commander. His heart beat faster. Scorpion! He clenched his fists and defiantly met the golden-brown eyes of his enemy. He wouldn’t go down easily. However, Scorpion simply waved a commanding hand, and the Fire Nation soldiers began to retreat.
“We’ve already got the one we need,” the wind carried the words to him. “The main objective is complete.”
Kuai Liang frowned, but he needed to tend to the wounded. He knelt beside Tomas, helping him up, and noticed a wound on his side. Water flowed from his hands, pulsing blue, healing the injury. The fighting comrades around them stopped, confused, watching the retreating enemy soldiers.
“Commander Hasashi, what about that bender? Doesn’t he meet the criteria too?”
“One is enough,” the voice carried a crooked smirk. “He’ll explain all the secrets to us.”
At that moment, as he watched the retreating soldiers, Kuai Liang didn’t know that that day marked the beginning of the end. For the Fire Nation had captured Bi-Han.

It was a baby, with golden eyes blinking up at him, slightly unfocused. There was something attached to her midsection, and he looked over at the woman.
“We found her this morning in the back gardens with a note attached to the basket. Her umbilical cord is still attached, so she can’t be older than a few days.” The girl explained.
He looked back down to the baby, whose eyes were still on him, and handed back the note. How could someone abandon such a sweet little baby? She had the roundest little face, and before he knew what he was doing, Zuko reached down to rub a finger across her cheek. The baby made a small cooing noise, and he swallowed.

summary: Zuko has an intensely sympathetic story and is a very sympathetic character. However, he also received far more grace from the narrative and the writers than any other villain and antagonist in ATLA or LoK. They took pains to present almost everything about him in about the most sympathetic possible way. This summary of Zuko's canon story is an effort to illustrate how people might imagine Zuko as a character if he, like Azula or the other antagonists, did not receive this grace and this sympathetic framing.

title: The Path
author: Woolfie
summary: Water. Earth. Fire. Air.My nation conquered much of the world over the course of a hundred years. The Avatar, master of all four elements, was thought to be lost, and though many hunted him, he eluded all over the decades that followed the Air Nomad genocide, carried out by my ancestor Fire Lord Sozin. But we were wrong. Aang, the last of his kind, returned and quickly learned the four elements. He defeated my father, Phoenix King Ozai and eliminated him without bloodshed while I was defeated by my brother, the banished Prince Zuko, on the cusp of my coronation as the new Fire Lord. Later I helped him search for our missing mother while I plotted for the throne, but when we found her and her new family, I ran. Soon after, I imitated the Kemurikage spirits to turn my brother’s rule into tyranny, with a group of rebellious daughters who I freed from the institution I eluded. But they abandoned me after I refused to save one of them from capture. Now I am alone.For all my life I’ve known my purpose; my destiny. The path is unknown. But I will find it again. I always do.

tags: Zuko has mad middle child energy
summary: There was a hand on his back, softly rubbing a soothing pattern against his shoulders. Zuko flinched away from the touch as much as he could while his stomach rebelled. It wasn't enough and the hand stayed where it was.It took a few minutes before he was able to stop dry heaving. When it was clear that nothing else was going to come up, Zuko rolled himself fully back onto the sleeping bag. His head hurt, it hurt a lot. Usually, his head felt fine after sleeping but today his brain felt expanded in his skull, pushing up against the inside and mashing all the squishy bits together.He wanted to get up, wanted to get away from whoever was tucking him back into the warmth of his sleeping bag. He whined low in his throat as the hands nudged his arms into the bag, the sound leaving his throat with a rasp. His eyes weren't focusing on anything, which wasn't out of the norm for his left side, but his right eye was fine. He should be fine. He was fine.(He wasn't fine.)“Are you okay?” A deep voice asked. (Zuko becomes a middle child, everyone is horrified by the new information that comes to light, and Hakoda wonders who he has to kill to make this scarred boy happy.

summary: Life isn't very fun or bountiful when you're the last descendant of a long gone nation. It is way less fun with a 100 year war waging just outside the icy walls of the Northern Water Tribe - where no human is safe, much less an airbender.So, from the moment Nerihn was born, her entire world was restricted within her home in the Tribe. As far as she and her mother were concerned, the boundaries of the world were the icy walls of the Tribe. As a result, Nerihn had never known anything beyond ice and snow and books - books that spoke of long lost beings like the Avatar and foreign concepts of freedom.But Nerihn was only allowed to read about the world beyond the walls - never to see or to touch. It was so frustrating to know of something so beautiful, yet always just beyond her reach. It always felt like life was just beyond her reach. Even the aspects of it she should be able to control, like her bending, she was never allowed to reach for and to relish in.She was to stay hidden, secret, contained. And her mother had been doing a wonderful job of doing just that. At least until the Avatar barged into the Northern Water Tribe and Nerihn finally saw the most dangerous thing of all - hope.

summary: Mai's icy fury burned brighter than the Fire Nation's forge. Betrayed by Zuko's cold indifference and seething with rage, she fled the stifling boat, seeking solace in the untamed wilderness of the southern seas. But fate had other plans - her battered skiff was swallowed by a crushing, ancient monolith of ice. In that heart-stopping moment, the ice parted to reveal a glowing, ethereal figure - the Avatar himself.Thrown together by circumstance, the disenchanted noblewoman and the young Avatar forged an unlikely alliance, their divergent personalities creating a volatile, captivating dynamic. With Aang's boundless energy and Mai's cool calculation, they navigated treacherous terrain, evading the relentless pursuit of the Fire Nation's forces. The journey was perilous, their own demons constantly haunting them, but an unbreakable bond began to form in the crucible of their shared trials.

"What do you want?" he snapped. Hanzo still hadn’t released his wrist. And Kuai Liang was still taking risks.
"Heal me." Hanzo’s gaze was strange. Feverish. He let go, exposing a wound on his shoulder.
Kuai Liang frowned.
"What?" The question slipped out, stupid and automatic. A smile tugged at his lips. This was absurd.
"I’m injured. And you’re a healer." Scorpion looked dead serious. "Heal me."
"Are you… mocking me?" His voice wavered. "I’m not your soldier, Hanzo. And you’re not my commander."
"Why not?" The firebender shrugged.
"You’re seriously asking?" He should have been furious at the audacity. Instead, he was just stunned. Bi-Han would have attacked by now—though no, his brother would never have gotten into this absurd situation in the first place. "You’re my enemy!"
